tested:
── vrnetlab catalogue expansion (O7a, war-room 2026-08-10) ────────────────────
5 genuinely-missing vrnetlab kinds, added after a real per-vendor audit of all
44 kinds hellt/vrnetlab actually ships (github.com/hellt/vrnetlab, live tree
read 2026-08-10 - README/Makefile/docker-compose content, NOT guessed - rule
33's "read the real source, don't guess" applied to vrnetlab's own upstream
since EVE-NG has no equivalent Docker-wrapped-VM template concept at all for
these; where a vendor's real EVE-NG QEMU template WOULD be the reference
(Juniper/Cisco/Arista/Nokia/Palo Alto/F5/... direct appliances), netplex
already has a native, template-verified direct-QEMU profile for that vendor -
see docs/reference/vrnetlab-catalogue-decisions-2026-08-10.md for the full
44-kind, evidence-per-vendor table. Wrapping an already-natively-supported
vendor in vrnetlab would be a straight regression (container + nested-QEMU
overhead for something that already boots direct) - only these 5 have NO
native path (no taxonomy tile, no curated device_profiles entry, no
device_registry.json fallback) anywhere in netplex today.
Image tags/resource floors are read directly from each vendor's real
vrnetlab Makefile (VENDOR/NAME -> IMG_REPOSITORY = vrnetlab/<vendor>_<name>,
lowercased) and README "System requirements" section - never invented.
Same generic infra the mikrotik entry above already uses covers all 5
automatically, no per-vendor frontend change needed: DockerProvider's
"vrnetlab/" privileged launch profile (docker_provider.py), the nested-serial
console bridge on 127.0.0.1:5000 (docker_exec.py), fixtures.ts's
DATA_IFACE_NAMING 'vrnetlab/' -> eth{1} rule, and Shell.tsx/StudioHome.tsx's
isVrnetlabImage()-driven RunChip/engine-pill/empty-state, all keyed on the
"vrnetlab/" image prefix, not a per-vendor allowlist.

reasons.image:
dell/dell_sonic/Makefile's own comment: a file named "dell-sonic-4.2.1.qcow2"
builds "vrnetlab/dell_sonic:4.2.1" - that exact example version used verbatim.
reasons.min_ram_mb:
dell/dell_sonic/README.md "System requirements": CPU 2 cores, RAM 4GB,
DISK ~3.2GB. min_ram set a step below the stated floor (matches the
mikrotik entry's pattern of min < default, since 4GB is Dell's own
recommended figure, not necessarily a hard minimum for the VM to boot).
reasons.boot_timeout_sec:
SONiC's own native profile (sonic-vs, below) already needs 300s; SONiC +
vrnetlab's nested-QEMU/health-probe overhead (mikrotik's +60s pattern)
budgets more.

settings.description: Dell Enterprise SONiC via vrnetlab (containerized QEMU wrapper). No native netplex profile exists for Dell's SONiC build specifically (community SONiC-VS is a different, unbranded build - kept separate, matching netplex's own precedent of keeping CSR1000v/Cat8000v distinct despite shared IOS-XE lineage).
